headline: GOLD REBOUNDS TO $4,570 — Retreating Dollar and Inflation Signals Push Metal Higher Tuesday
snippet: Gold spot rose to $4,570.50/oz Tuesday, up $30.60 (+0.67%), as a weakening U.S. dollar and persistent inflation signals boosted precious metals across global markets. Gold is now trading $1,334/oz higher year-over-year — a 25%+ gain since early 2025.

headline: MIN REBOOTS BALD HILL — Mineral Resources Restarts WA Lithium Mine After 18-Month Shutdown as Prices Recover
snippet: Mineral Resources (ASX: MIN) will restart its 165,000 dmt/yr Bald Hill spodumene mine in Western Australia, with crushing and mining beginning in June and the first shipment from Port of Esperance due Q1 FY27. At a $20M restart cost, MinRes will become the only company globally operating three hard-rock lithium mines simultaneously.

headline: COPPER POSTS THIRD STRAIGHT LOSS — China Retail and Industrial Data Miss Drags Futures Below $6.20/lb
snippet: China copper scrap prices fell up to CNY 2,000/mt on May 18 after retail sales, industrial production, and fixed asset investment all missed consensus, deepening demand concerns in the world's largest copper consumer. Copper futures slipped below $6.20/lb for a third consecutive session, their lowest in nearly two weeks.

headline: CHINA SILVER IMPORTS TOP 790 TONNES IN Q1 — Solar Manufacturing Displaces EVs as Dominant Demand Driver
snippet: China imported more than 790 tonnes of silver in Q1 2026, with solar panel manufacturing overtaking EV batteries as the primary industrial demand driver, per GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT analysis. The data reinforces a structural supply deficit now in its sixth consecutive year as mine production fails to keep pace.

headline: DAKOTA GOLD HITS 1.49 G/T OVER 38M — Richmond Hill Infill 85% Complete, South Dakota PFS on Track for H2
snippet: Dakota Gold (NYSE American: DC) intersected 1.49 g/t Au and 8.13 g/t Ag over 38.1 metres in infill drilling at its Richmond Hill project in South Dakota, part of a 109-hole, 15,481-metre 2026 campaign now over 85% complete. A preliminary feasibility study is on track for H2 2026, with full feasibility targeted for H1 2027.

headline: SILVER STALLS AT $77 — Stop Chasing the Number; January's $121 ATH Left a Persistent Bearish Overhang
snippet: After a $121.64 all-time high in January and a sustained correction, silver is consolidating in a $70–$80 range with the May 11 tariff-truce bounce already fading. Analysts urge patience over momentum-chasing, flagging a potential re-test of the $70 zone as the better entry before the next structural leg higher.

headline: URANIUM LONG-TERM CONTRACTS BREAK $150/LB — Utilities Quietly Securing Supply as Spot Holds Near $86
snippet: While U3O8 spot held near $86/lb in mid-May, the long-term contract market — where utilities sign multi-year supply deals — has broken to $150/lb, a historic divergence analysts call a fundamental re-rating of nuclear fuel. Drivers include 70 new reactors under construction globally and U.S. tech giants contracting for small modular reactor power.

headline: NdPr OXIDE CRASHES 21% IN APRIL — Rare Earths Retreat to $99/kg But Remain 88% Higher Year-to-Date
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April to $99.61/kg — the sharpest monthly decline since the Q1 rally began from $53/kg in January — as post-Trump-Xi summit tariff enthusiasm faded. Analysts see consolidation in a $95–$115/kg range through Q2 2026, with longer-term demand from EV motors and wind turbines intact.

headline: GOLD MINERS FINALLY OUTPACING BULLION — Valuation Gap Closing as Producer Margins Hit Multi-Year Highs
snippet: With gold trading above $4,500/oz, gold mining equities are beginning to close a decade-long valuation discount relative to the metal as producer margins reach multi-year highs. Analysts point to operational improvements, M&A consolidation tailwinds, and historical undervaluation as the setup for a sustained re-rating of senior and mid-tier producers.

headline: LITHIUM DOUBLED IN Q1 — Zimbabwe Export Ban and Energy Storage Boom Push Carbonate to $26,278/t
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate nearly doubled in Q1 2026 to $26,278/t after Zimbabwe's February suspension of raw mineral exports tightened an already constrained market. Energy storage systems now account for 31% of global LCE demand — up from 23% in 2025 — reinforcing the structural case for junior lithium developers.
